title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the Hugging Face (HF) repos plantcad/PlantCAD2_fine_tuning_tasks and PlantCAD2_zero_shot_tasks with file sizes. Downloaded and opened all 6 translation parquet files (absolute and on/off; 21,894 train / 5,492 validation / 39,035 test rows, matching the HF README) plus the 12,249-row expression validation file. Confirmed: 500-bp sequences present, no nulls, no duplicate genes, train = Arabidopsis (AT gene IDs, chr 1-5), test = maize (Zm00001eb IDs, chr 1-10); label = log10(tpm+1) exactly (Spearman 1.0, checked arithmetic); on/off label is a TPM threshold (off max 0.30 log units). Expression files carry orthogroup and genome columns.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the translation 'tpm' is ribosome profiling (ribo-seq) from two cited studies, that sequences are 500 bp upstream of the start codon, that cross-species absolute translation regression 'was less effective', and the expression scores (AUROC 0.8455, Spearman 0.6455) — from the bioRxiv v4 full text via WebFetch, not the Europe PMC text (network lookup failed). Paper-side row counts not verified; no Apache licence tag on the fine-tuning repo (zero-shot repo is Apache-2.0).

a1_downloadable.note: Public, ungated HF parquet; downloaded translation files directly without login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Label is a 'label' column in every task file (checked); a 'tpm' column duplicates it and must be dropped.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full DNA sequence strings in the 'sequence' column (500 bp translation, 2,048 bp expression), no lookups needed (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Units not documented in README, but I verified label = log10(TPM+1) exactly from the tpm column; consistent across splits.

a5_enough_rows.note: Translation task: 21,894 train + 5,492 val + 39,035 maize test rows (counted). Expression tasks have ~1.9M rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~33 MB for translation task; expression/chromatin tasks 2-10 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Translation task trivially fits; larger tasks need subsetting. PlantCAD2 itself (Mamba2) realistically needs a CUDA GPU, so a CPU backbone like DNABERT-2 would be used.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Downloaded row counts match HF README metadata exactly; paper's own counts not retrieved.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is measured ribo-seq abundance (per paper), log-transformed; not a model output. Leakage only via the redundant tpm column.

B1.why: One parquet table per split per task; gene, sequence, label in same rows (checked).

B2.why: Parquet parsed first try with pandas+pyarrow (checked).

B3.why: Arabidopsis and maize ribo-seq from two different studies; TPM scales not cross-normalised (paper text).

B4.why: Zero-TPM genes are floor values: 50% of maize test labels are exactly 0 (checked).

B5.why: No duplicate gene IDs in any split (checked).

B6.why: README gives column types only; units and assay inferred from paper and arithmetic.

C1.why: Transfer question (Arabidopsis to maize) informative either way, but authors already report it partly.

C2.why: PlantCAD2, AgroNT, PlantCaduceus all open and evaluated on this exact cross-species split.

C3.why: Weak 'better' angle: test whether frozen embeddings beat k-mer baselines where authors say transfer fails.

C4.why: Ribo-seq is costly per species, but annotation-level translation calls are not a pressing bottleneck.

C5.why: Published PlantCAD2/AgroNT numbers on same split (Supplemental Table 10 per paper).

D1.why: PlantCAD2 and DNABERT-2 weights open on HF (PlantCAD2 Apache-2.0 tag seen).

D2.why: PlantCAD2 Mamba2 kernels need GPU; CPU route uses DNABERT-2 embeddings, 66k short sequences.

D3.why: Apache-2.0 on PlantCAD2 models and zero-shot data (HF tags checked).

E1.why: Built-in cross-species split: train Arabidopsis, test maize (checked).

E2.why: Chromosomes (5 Arabidopsis, 10 maize) usable as hold-out groups (checked).

E3.why: Global mean / majority class dummy computable; 41% positives in maize test (checked).

E4.why: No replicate columns; ribo-seq noise not estimable from files.

E5.why: Upstream ORFs in 5' leaders known to lower translation; must be recovered.

E6.why: Label shuffle and sequence-shuffle controls trivially runnable.

E7.why: Maize test is an independent study and species (paper text).

E8.why: Reported PlantCAD2 AUROC on maize translation on/off reproducible with released weights (GPU).

G1.why: TAIR AGI and maize B73 v5 gene IDs present (checked).

G2.why: Matched RNA-seq to compute translation efficiency plausible (e.g. source studies), not yet located.

G3.why: One row per gene, clean gene-ID join.

G4.why: Adding mRNA levels would separate translation control from transcription; marginal beyond paper.

H1.why: Both translated and untranslated genes included; 36% off in Arabidopsis train (checked).

H2.why: Two species, one study each, leaf tissue only.

H4.why: Paper flags ribo-seq noise; does not flag ribo-seq tracking mRNA level.

I1.why: Plant genomics / DNA language model community; no specific decision-maker.

I2.why: Would inform choice of backbone for crop annotation, marginally.

I3.why: AUROC/Spearman roughly aligned to genome-annotation use.

I4.why: k-mer models may do nearly as well; untested.

J1.why: Real transfer learning, embeddings, cross-species evaluation.

J2.why: Some domain intuition needed on plant translation regulation.

J3.why: k-mer baseline vs embedding comparison shareable at each step.

J4.why: Roughly one to two weekends; not formally set.

existing_models.name: PlantCAD2 (Mamba2 DNA language model, 88M-694M params, 2025/2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Arabidopsis-trained, maize-tested translation on/off and absolute (exact values in Supplemental Table 10, not retrieved); expression on/off AUROC 0.8455, absolute Spearman 0.6455 on maize NAM genomes.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-species regression of absolute translation levels was less effective, attributed to ribo-seq noise; regulatory elements beyond 8 kb.

existing_models.name: AgroNT (1B-parameter plant Nucleotide Transformer, 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Same cross-species benchmarks with LoRA (low-rank adapter) fine-tuning; beaten by PlantCAD2 per paper.

existing_models.name: PlantCaduceus (PlantCAD v1, 512-bp context, PNAS 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Arabidopsis-to-maize transfer on splice/start/stop site tasks; not retrieved for translation.

existing_models.name: PlantCaduceus-embedding sequence-to-expression models across 17 species (bioRxiv 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to beat PhytoExpr on cross-species expression; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 (CPU-friendly DNA language model) for frozen embeddings; PlantCAD2-Small as GPU comparison
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop for DNABERT-2 on 66k x 500 bp; PlantCAD2 needs a CUDA GPU for Mamba2 kernels

integration.partner_dataset: Matched leaf RNA-seq from the same Arabidopsis and maize ribo-seq studies (not yet located)
integration.join_key: TAIR AGI / maize B73 v5 gene ID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does upstream sequence predict translation efficiency (ribosomes per mRNA) across species, or only how much mRNA is there?

controls.positive_control: Upstream ORF count in the 500-bp leader should correlate negatively with translation; trivially, predicting GC content from sequence.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within chromosome; dinucleotide-shuffled sequences should collapse to dummy.
controls.external_validation: Maize test set is a separate species and study (built in).

honest_claim_h3: Predicts whether a maize gene has detectable leaf ribosome-profiling signal from its 500-bp upstream sequence, using a model trained on one Arabidopsis leaf study — which largely reflects mRNA abundance, not translation control.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA just upstream of a plant gene's start codon to predict how much it is translated, training in Arabidopsis and testing in maize.
plain_idea.train_on: 21,894 Arabidopsis genes, each a 500-letter DNA sequence upstream of the start codon (verified); tested on 39,035 maize genes.
plain_idea.predict: Ribosome footprint abundance (log TPM, transcripts per million) or on/off, measured by ribosome profiling sequencing in leaves in two published studies.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tells plant genomics groups whether cheap frozen DNA-model embeddings transfer across 160 million years of divergence for translation, where the PlantCAD2 authors report regression transfer fails.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use exactly the PlantCAD2 authors' benchmark files (21,894 train, 39,035 test); no extra data.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements in the files, so no basis for calibrated per-gene uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: PlantCAD2 (2025/2026, LoRA, honest cross-species split) is strong overall, but its own authors say absolute translation transfer is weak, leaving room for simple baselines.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible joined dataset measuring the same quantity identified; matched RNA-seq would change the target to translation efficiency.

label_elsewhere.sources: Plant ribo-seq studies scattered in GEO/SRA and translatome databases (known resources, not searched); no single joinable table.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Species gene ID (TAIR AGI, maize B73 v5)
label_elsewhere.why: Additional ribo-seq from other plants could give a third test species, but would need reprocessing from raw reads.

ambitious.why: Would need showing frozen embeddings plus mRNA-aware targets solve cross-species translation prediction where PlantCAD2 fails.

realistic.why: Benchmark note comparing k-mer, DNABERT-2 and PlantCAD2 on cross-species translation transfer.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus MLCB / ICLR GEM workshop
fallback.why: Negative result that frozen DNA models add little over k-mers for plant translation is still shareable.

pitch.headline: A clean, 33 MB Arabidopsis-to-maize translation benchmark with sequences and labels in one parquet table, ready to model.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Built-in cross-species split: 21,894 Arabidopsis training genes, 39,035 maize test genes, zero duplicates, zero nulls (checked); ribo-seq origin is from the paper only.
pitch.the_win: A CPU frozen-embedding model matching PlantCAD2's published maize translation on/off AUROC (exact value in Supplemental Table 10, not retrieved) without a GPU.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Learn whether 500-bp upstream sequence carries transferable translation signal beyond k-mer composition, or whether these labels mostly track mRNA abundance.
pitch.who_wants_it: The PlantCAD/Kuleshov and Buckler groups and crop-genome annotators choosing whether GPU-heavy plant DNA models are needed.

ml_idea: Embed the 66k 500-bp upstream sequences once with DNABERT-2 on CPU, fit logistic/ridge heads on Arabidopsis, test on maize; compare with 6-mer counts, upstream-ORF features and PlantCAD2's published numbers; drop the leaking tpm column.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: DNABERT-2 at ~10-20 sequences/s for 500 bp on CPU over 66k sequences; heads are linear models on 768-d features.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit a 6-mer logistic regression on Arabidopsis and score maize on/off AUROC; if it matches PlantCAD2's published value, the backbone story is dead.

verdict_reason: Data is clean and laptop-sized, but it is the PlantCAD2 authors' own benchmark with open, honestly evaluated models already on it (C2 = 0), labels from two studies only, and the best backbone needs a GPU; only a small benchmark note is realistic.
